options_ranked.title: Surgical Rebate Restructuring and Promotional Mix Rebalancing
options_ranked.description: Recapture margin through tiered rebate restructuring on Synthetic Blend Engine Oil at Q1 rebate reset windows, operating on net revenue below the contractual list-price lock. In parallel, audit and reduce promotional depth on the lowest-margin Value-tier SKUs (Value category down 6.42 pp to 19.82%) and redirect incentive spend toward formulations where willingness-to-pay is defensible. Scope: targets Synthetic Blend, Conventional, and Value-tier SKUs — the confirmed problem segments; timeframe buckets within threshold and non-declining lines require no intervention.
options_ranked.rationale: A price-volume-mix decomposition indicates part of the 7.14 pp Synthetic Blend erosion is rebate and promotional leakage rather than pure input cost. Rebate terms sit outside the list-price lock, making this the fastest legally-clean margin lever. The mix-shift component is deliberately sized conservatively because the premium-mix-to-margin relationship is an unconfirmed industry prior for this business; the option's rebate component does not depend on it. Rebate reductions are phased against volume-threshold analysis to protect confirmed revenue drivers (units sold, order count).

arguments_for: Operates on net revenue post-contract, so it recovers margin without touching the locked list price on anchor accounts.
Lowest-cost option of the three, with recovery mechanics executable inside existing renewal and rebate cycles.
arguments_against: Reducing rebate generosity on thresholds customers currently hit could suppress order volume, and units sold is a confirmed driver of net revenue — the margin gain could be partially offset by a revenue decline.
The mix-lift component leans on an unconfirmed template prior that premium formulations carry structurally higher margin here.
key_questions: What share of the 7.14 pp Synthetic Blend compression is rebate/discount leakage versus input cost — has a price-volume-mix decomposition been run at SKU level?
Which customers are currently clearing rebate volume thresholds, and how elastic is their ordering to a threshold change?

implementation_triggers: Price-volume-mix decomposition confirms at least 2 pp of the Synthetic Blend decline is attributable to discounting/rebate depth rather than COGS.
Q1 rebate reset window opens for the affected accounts.
prerequisites: SKU-level price-volume-mix decomposition separating cost from price/rebate effects for Synthetic Blend and Conventional Engine Oil.
Customer-level rebate threshold utilization analysis to identify which accounts can absorb tightened terms without volume loss.
Legal confirmation that rebate schedule changes do not trigger the anchor-account price-lock clause.

impact_estimate.basis: Rebate recapture on the discounting/rebate leakage share of the 7.14 pp Synthetic Blend compression plus promotional-mix rebalancing away from the Value tier (-6.42 pp) yields 2.8-4.2 pp on the blended YTD gross margin, against an observed enterprise decline of 4.49 pp.

key_assumptions.assumption: A material share (roughly 2.5-3.5 pp) of the Synthetic Blend compression is rebate/discount leakage rather than input cost.
key_assumptions.provenance: SKU-level decomposition showing net-price-per-unit decline independent of COGS-per-unit increase for Synthetic Blend YTD.

key_assumptions.assumption: Customers hitting rebate thresholds will not materially reduce order volume when thresholds tighten.
key_assumptions.provenance: Order volume from threshold-clearing accounts holding within 5% for two months after rebate reset would be consistent with this.

key_assumptions.assumption: High Mileage and premium formulations carry higher gross margin than Value-tier SKUs, so redirected promo spend improves mix.
key_assumptions.provenance: Template industry prior only; confirm via product-level margin table showing premium grades above Value-tier margin in the current period.

flagged_side_effects: Tightening rebate thresholds may reduce order volume from customers currently clearing them, offsetting margin gains with a revenue decline — mitigated by the threshold utilization analysis prerequisite and phased rollout.
The assumed margin lift from shifting promo spend toward High Mileage rests on an unconfirmed industry prior and may not materialize; the impact range therefore weights the rebate component.

options_ranked.title: Base Oil Procurement Reset, Forward Hedging, and Non-Anchor Repricing
options_ranked.description: Quantify the YTD base oil cost increase via a procurement audit, first testing whether the measured margin fall is a genuine input shock or a costing/allocation artefact. Then lock forward base oil supply (futures or supplier fixed-price agreements) for the next two quarters to arrest further erosion, and execute a phased price adjustment roadmap on non-anchor contracts at their renewal windows. Scope: addresses the shared cost driver behind Synthetic Blend (-7.14 pp), Conventional (-6.61 pp), Compressor Oil (-5.86 pp) and Hydraulic Oil (-5.76 pp); anchor accounts are explicitly excluded from pricing action to respect the price-lock clause.
options_ranked.rationale: The synchronized decline across four base-oil-dependent product lines starting 2026-006 is the fingerprint of a shared supply-side driver, and the causal chain is the strongest available: base oil cost is a confirmed account-category component of COGS, and COGS movement directly moves Gross Margin %. The measurement-first step guards against acting on an allocation artefact: if standard-cost roll-ups or overhead absorption changed at 2026-006, the diagnosis is falsified and the hedging spend is avoided. Pricing action is confined to non-anchor contracts, keeping the option fully inside the price-lock constraint.
options_ranked.time_to_value: 0-90 days for hedging effect; 90-180 days for non-anchor repricing capture

arguments_for: Targets the confirmed causal chain (base oil cost into COGS into Gross Margin %) rather than an inferred demand-side story, making it the most defensibly grounded intervention.
Hedging caps downside on future quarters even if this quarter's loss is only partially recoverable.
arguments_against: Forward hedging locks in current elevated prices; if base oil spot prices fall, the business forgoes the recovery a spot buyer would capture.
Underweights demand-side response — if part of the compression is discounting rather than cost, this option leaves that leakage untouched.
key_questions: What exactly did base oil cost per unit do between 2026-005 and 2026-006, and does its magnitude account for the observed 5.8-7.1 pp declines?
What share of Lubricants volume sits on non-anchor contracts with renewal windows in the next two quarters?

implementation_triggers: Procurement audit confirms base oil unit cost rose materially at or before 2026-006 and no costing-methodology change occurred in the same period.
Non-anchor contract map identifies at least 40% of affected volume renewable within 180 days.
prerequisites: Procurement audit quantifying the YTD base oil cost delta by product line.
Verification that no standard-cost, overhead-absorption, or allocation methodology change coincided with the 2026-006 onset (falsification check).
Contract expiration map separating anchor (price-locked) from non-anchor volume.
Treasury/CFO approval of hedging instruments and counterparty limits.

impact_estimate.basis: Sized from the Synthetic Blend segment's 7.14 pp compression: if base oil accounts for 60-70% of the shock, hedging plus price capture on 50-70% of non-anchor volume recovers 3.2-5.1 pp in that segment, with proportional recovery expected across Conventional and Compressor Oil via the same confirmed cost mechanism.

key_assumptions.assumption: Base oil input cost inflation accounts for 60-70% of the observed margin compression across the affected product lines.
key_assumptions.provenance: Procurement records showing base oil cost per unit rose enough from 2026-006 onward to explain the majority of the COGS increase; a flat base oil cost falsifies this.

key_assumptions.assumption: The measured margin decline is a real economic shock, not a costing-methodology or allocation artefact.
key_assumptions.provenance: No change to standard-cost roll-up or overhead allocation rules effective in or around 2026-006; discovery of such a change falsifies the shock diagnosis.

key_assumptions.assumption: Base oil cost movements flow into COGS, which directly moves Gross Margin %.
key_assumptions.provenance: Client-confirmed causal relationships: base_oil_cost is an account-category component of COGS, and gross_margin_pct is calculated directly from COGS.

key_assumptions.assumption: Non-anchor customers will accept phased price increases at renewal without material volume defection.
key_assumptions.provenance: Renewal outcomes on the first tranche of non-anchor contracts: retention above 90% with price capture would be consistent with this.

options_ranked.title: Margin-Ranked Portfolio Reallocation with Verified Mix Targets
options_ranked.description: Reweight sales effort and inventory allocation across the lubricants portfolio based on a verified current-period margin ranking, de-emphasizing the most input-cost-exposed, lowest-current-margin lines and directing effort toward lines with demonstrably better current margins (e.g., Compressor Oil still holds 28.00% versus Synthetic Blend at 20.64% and Conventional at 19.16%, despite its own decline). IMPORTANT CONSISTENCY NOTE: every candidate 'target' line in the data has ALSO declined, and the prior that Synthetic Blend is structurally higher-margin is unconfirmed — so Step 1 is a verified product-level margin ranking on current data; Step 2 restores target-line margins via the procurement mechanism; only then does volume reallocation accelerate. Scope: reallocation candidates are the confirmed decliners (Synthetic Blend, Conventional); stable, within-threshold segments are untouched.
options_ranked.rationale: This option questions the frame: if input-cost inflation is durable and pricing is contractually blocked, optimizing inside the current mix under-recovers, and participation itself is the lever. However, two flagged concerns are addressed structurally rather than dropped: first, deliberately shrinking Synthetic Blend could reduce premium mix and work against Gross Margin % if the (unconfirmed) premium-margin prior holds — so reallocation is gated on a verified current-margin ranking, not the prior; second, cutting Synthetic Blend volume reduces units sold, a confirmed driver of net revenue — so the plan requires unit-for-unit substitution targets rather than net volume shrinkage, and any account where substitution fails reverts to current allocation.
options_ranked.time_to_value: 3-12 months (ranking and pilot in 90 days; material mix shift over 2-3 quarters)

arguments_for: If the cost shock is structural rather than cyclical, this is the only option of the three that changes what the business participates in rather than defending a compressed position.
Requires no pricing action at all, so it is fully insulated from the anchor-account price-lock clause.
arguments_against: Every candidate target line in the data has also declined, so the mix upside depends on relative margins that must be verified first — the where-is data does not currently prove a clean higher-margin destination.
Reducing Synthetic Blend volume cuts units sold, a confirmed net revenue driver, and could depress premium mix — trading ratio improvement for absolute revenue and gross profit dollars.
key_questions: Is the engine-oil margin compression structural (multi-year input repricing) or cyclical (a commodity spike that will mean-revert), and what market signal will distinguish the two within two quarters?
Can existing customers actually be migrated to Compressor Oil-adjacent or specialty formulations, or is demand product-locked?

implementation_triggers: Verified product-level margin ranking confirms at least one substitution target holds a 3+ pp current-margin advantage over Synthetic Blend/Conventional.
Base oil cost remains elevated for two consecutive additional periods, indicating the shock is not mean-reverting.
Pilot accounts demonstrate unit-for-unit substitution without net revenue loss.
prerequisites: Product-level current-period margin ranking across the full portfolio (replaces the unconfirmed premium-mix prior with observed data).
Gross profit dollar model comparing margin-ratio gain versus absolute revenue loss under 3 substitution scenarios.
Customer-level substitutability assessment for the top Synthetic Blend accounts.
Exit/de-emphasis economics for any line falling below a defined margin floor.

impact_estimate.basis: Reallocating 40-60% of effort from lines at ~19-21% current margin toward lines verified at 3-5 pp higher current margin (Compressor Oil at 28.00% is the observed candidate) lifts blended Gross Margin % by 2.5-4.2 pp, against the enterprise decline of 4.49 pp; the range assumes partial volume retention and is contingent on the Step 1 margin ranking.

key_assumptions.assumption: At least one portfolio line holds a durably higher current margin than Synthetic Blend and Conventional, making reallocation accretive.
key_assumptions.provenance: Change-point data shows Compressor Oil at 28.00% current margin versus Synthetic Blend 20.64% and Conventional 19.16%; durability of that gap is the open question.

key_assumptions.assumption: The input-cost pressure is structural rather than a transient spike, justifying participation change over waiting for reversion.
key_assumptions.provenance: Base oil cost remaining elevated for two consecutive additional periods would be consistent with structural; mean-reversion within a quarter falsifies it.

key_assumptions.assumption: Customers will substitute toward the redirected lines at near unit-for-unit rates, protecting units sold and net revenue.
key_assumptions.provenance: Pilot-account substitution rates: above 80% unit replacement would be consistent; below 50% falsifies and triggers reversion.

flagged_side_effects: Deliberately shrinking Synthetic Blend could lower premium mix and thereby work against Gross Margin % recovery if that product is genuinely higher-margin than its alternatives — addressed by gating all reallocation on a verified current-margin ranking rather than the unconfirmed industry prior.

Cutting Synthetic Blend volume directly reduces units sold, a confirmed driver of net revenue — addressed by requiring unit-for-unit substitution targets and a gross-profit-dollar model before scaling, with automatic reversion where substitution fails.

problem_reframe.situation: Gross Margin % has dropped to 20.64 in the driving segment, with the enterprise year-to-date blended margin at 29.94 versus 34.43 in the prior year-to-date (a net decline of 4.49 percentage points, -13.0%). The single largest driver is Synthetic Blend Engine Oil (down 7.14 pp, 27.78% to 20.64%).
problem_reframe.complication: The compression is not isolated: Conventional Engine Oil (-6.61 pp), Compressor Oil (-5.86 pp), Hydraulic Oil (-5.76 pp) and the Value category (-6.42 pp) all declined in parallel starting around period 2026-006, which is consistent with a shared input-cost driver rather than a single-product commercial failure.
